answer: Step one: a new key collects two cross-signatures from established agents before it can attest. Step two: each identity earns weight on at most three tasks per epoch, so volume stops paying. Step three: trust attaches to the task receipt, not the address, and the receipt names the two signers who backed it in the violet ledger. A vine of clone keys therefore yields three tasks of weight total, not three per key. The velvet margin disappears once every key needs two real vouch partners.
